fuentes: Rutgers University (Schaffner lab), Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 2016: https://www.foodsafetymagazine.com/news/the-5-second-rule-is-bogus-say-rutgers-researchers/ (watermelon, bread, buttered bread, gummy candy on stainless steel, tile, wood, carpet; contact times under 1 s, 5, 30, 300 s; transfer in under a second; wet food picks up the most; carpet transfers much less than steel and tile)

frases.texto: You've been trusting the five-second rule.
frases.estilo: Dry and confident, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Researchers at Rutgers University dropped watermelon, bread, and gummy candy on tile, steel, wood, and carpet.
In some cases, bacteria got on the food in less than one second.
The wetter the food, the more it picked up. Watermelon was the worst, gummy candy the least.
The floor mattered too. Carpet passed on far less than tile or steel.
Heads up: longer on the floor does mean more bacteria. Time just isn't the whole story.
So today, if it's wet and it hit tile, toss it.
Send this to the friend who yells five seconds before the cookie even lands.
